newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee court halts incorporations temporarily.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee court halts incorporations temporarily.

text.p: A Tennessee Chancery Court Judge issued an order Monday temporarily halting municipal incorporations because of a challenge of the state's new incorporation law.
The state agreed to the order by Chancellor Ellen Hobbs Lyle in Davidson County, which delays incorporation elections at least until Lyle hears a reqest for an injunction on Aug 14.
"We're very happy about this. It freezes everything right in its tracks until the constitutionality of this act can be decided," Joe Sweat, executive director of the Tennessee Municipal League, said.
The league and several municipalities, including City of Memphis, challenged the constitutionality of the new law in a lawsuit filed on Friday.
The law made it possible to form a municipality right outside an existing city's borders. It reduced from 1,500 to 255 the number of residents required for incorporation.
The old law gave cities priority when they sought to annex a smaller neighbor. The new version gives priority to the area seeking incorporation.
The amendment to the state's annexation law took effect in April and will last for only one year.

The plaintiffs said it would unconstitutionally restrict the growth of existing cities and siphon from counties a portion of sales-tax revenues that are divided among localities where the tax is collected.
Since the law took effect, petitions have been filed to incorporate four new towns in East Shelby County and others have been filed elsewhere in the state.
